To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) peg-IFN plus ribavirin is well-tolerated and effective in HIV/HCV co-infected patients; (ii) severe side effects, including pancreatitis, can occur; and (iii) sustained response is less frequent than in HCV-moninfected individuals, and relapses are common.

peg-IFN plus ribavirin is a relatively well-tolerable and efficacious treatment for chronic hepatitis C infection in HIV-infected persons, although the response rate is lower than that seen with HCV-monoinfection and new side-effects, such as pancreatitis and severe body weight loss, may occur.

Treatment with pegIFN and ribavairn is relatively well tolerated in HIV/HCV co-infected patients, but the sustained response rate is significantly lower compared to HCV monoinfected individuals, mainly due to the high relapse rate.
